subject: openCR AIC discrepancy between (printed) output of fitted model and AIC() function

messages.author: cca1214dbfb1139e
messages.subject: openCR AIC discrepancy between (printed) output of fitted model and AIC() function
parts:
Dear all,

It appears that, in openCR, often the AIC values of the printed model output and the AIC function do not agree perfectly.

Its a minor thing, but I was wondering which AIC value should be trusted more? I guess the AIC from the AIC function? Below is an example what I mean.

Thanks a lot in Advance
Lukas

#openCR-examples _ example
#from page 2 CJS models
library(openCR)

#differing AIC values when using AIC() or directly from printed output

#Example model
model1<-openCR.fit(microtusFMCH, model = list(phi ~ sex+t, p ~ 1))

#AIC when just looking at the output of model1 is AICc = 751.6394
model1

# Analysis type   :  CJS
# Model           :  p~1 phi~sex + t
# Fixed (real)    :  none
# N parameters    :  7
# Log likelihood  :  -368.633
# AIC             :  751.266
# AICc            :  751.6394

#AICc when using AIC() is 753.266
AIC(model1)

#which of the two AIC values should be reported? I guess the one from the AIC function?

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: openCR AIC discrepancy between (printed) output of fitted model and AIC() function
parts:
Hi Lukas
This is a bit complicated. First, the AIC values are identical, only the AICc values differ. AICc depends on the sample size n, for which there is not strong theory or universal agreement - one reason for preferring AIC as your criterion (there are others).

The difference is because AIC.openCR() has an argument n that defaults to NULL and gives AICc = AIC+2, whereas print.openCR() assumes n = number of different individuals and computes AICc internally - in the Microtus example n = 308 and AICc is close to AIC.

Try AIC(model1, n = 308).

This needs to be tidied up or at least better documented. Thanks for pointing it out.

Murray
